title: Slot-based quota windows with carryover for reserved capacity
creator: Laura Chen
description: Problem: Reserved capacity customers are seeing opaque failures and unexpected throttles near boundary times (midnight local and subscription boundaries) because current monthly/daily resets are coarse and assume uniform traffic. This causes poor UX for bursty tenants and creates large reconciliation overhead for billing. Goal: Introduce deterministic slot-based quota windows (configurable slot size e.g., 1h, 4h, 24h) with optional carryover credits that let unused capacity from previous slots be consumed in the following slot, capped by a configurable max carryover. This should work for hosted and dedicated pools and integrate with reserved capacity lease/commit accounting. Constraints: must preserve billing correctness, be auditable (per-slot ledger), respect tenant timezones and reserved pool isolation, and minimize additional read/write load on quota store. Backward compatibility: default behavior for existing tenants remains unchanged. New behavior gated behind feature flag and tenant opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New slot-based quota policy can be configured per-tenant with slot_size_hours and carryover_max_percent settings
2) For an opt-in tenant, unused tokens from slot T can be consumed in slot T+1 up to carryover_max_percent and overage is rejected/charged according to existing reserved-capacity billing rules
3) Quota ledger exposes per-slot entries in billing telemetry and can be queried for audits (API + console panel)
4) No regression in latency for token-metering hot paths (+/- 2ms p99), and overall storage writes < 1.5x current baseline under representative load
5) End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout demonstrate correct behavior across DST boundary and tenant timezone offsets
design_decisions: Per-slot ledger vs continuous window: choose discrete slots to keep bookkeeping simple and auditable; avoids heavy sliding-window counters
Carryover semantics: carryover is implemented as an additive credit bucket with a capped ceiling defined as carryover_max_percent of slot capacity
Storage strategy: leverage existing quota ledger table with a compact slot key (tenant_id, slot_start_unix) to avoid schema churn; write-on-change instead of every request to reduce R/W pressure
Enforcement point: enforcement stays in the quota service (thin client-side token fetch + fast local cache) to keep runtime latency low and allow shared enforcement between hosted and dedicated
Time alignment: use tenant-configured timezone for slot boundaries; slot_start computed from UTC offset to keep single source-of-truth for cross-region reconciliation
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: add slot_start_unix and carryover_credit fields to quota ledger table (migration script + backfill for last 30 days)
2) Quota service: implement slot calculator util and carryover credit manager; ensure idempotent writes for concurrent token consumption
3) API: extend tenant quota config APIs to accept slot_size_hours and carryover_max_percent; add opt-in flag
4) Client SDK: expose opt-in helper and local cache awareness for slot boundaries
5) Telemetry: emit slot.metrics for consumed, available, carryover_used, and cancelled_tokens
6) Testing: unit tests for slot math, integration tests with billing pipeline, and chaos tests across timezone/dst transitions
7) Rollout: behind feature flag, internal canary tenants -> small set of paid customers -> full opt-in availability
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal staging test with synthetic tenants and replayed traffic (1 week)
Phase 1: internal canary with 3 Redwood teams using real traffic (2 weeks)
Phase 2: invite-only paid customers (5 customers) monitor for 30 days
Phase 3: GA opt-in for all reserved-capacity tenants
Feature flag: enable via tenant config and global kill-switch for emergency rollback
test_plan: Unit tests: slot boundary math, carryover cap enforcement, concurrent token consumption idempotency
Integration: full request flow through quota service, ledger writes, billing aggregation, and console display
Property tests: random slot sizes, random carryover percents, simulated burst patterns
DST/timezone tests: simulate tenants in UTC+14 and UTC-12 across month boundary
Performance: benchmark quota path p99 under production-like QPS with and without carryover enabled
